## Introduction

This is the Python twin of `wagepan_fixest.Rmd`. We estimate a **Mincer-type wage
equation** on the panel dataset `wagepan`:

$$
\ln(wage_{it}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 educ_i + \beta_2 exper_{it} + \beta_3 exper^2_{it} + u_{it}
$$

where $i$ indexes individuals and $t$ indexes years, and we compare **different
standard errors**:

- Classical (homoskedastic)
- Robust (heteroskedasticity-consistent)
- Clustered by individual
- Two-way clustered by individual and year

Setup (one time): `pip install pyfixest wooldridge` (or `uv pip install ...`).

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import pyfixest as pf
import wooldridge

wagepan = wooldridge.data("wagepan")
wagepan[["nr", "year", "lwage", "educ", "exper", "expersq"]].head()
```

Variables:

- `lwage`: log wage
- `educ`: years of education
- `exper`: work experience
- `expersq`: experience squared
- `nr`: individual ID
- `year`: calendar year

## Baseline Regression

We estimate without fixed effects (classical standard errors):

```{python}
mod1 = pf.feols("lwage ~ educ + exper + expersq", data=wagepan)
mod1.summary()
```

## Individual Fixed Effects

Usually, we add **individual fixed effects**. The formula syntax is the same as
`fixest`: everything after `|` is absorbed as a fixed effect. Note that `educ` drops
out --- it does not vary within person.

```{python}
mod2 = pf.feols("lwage ~ exper + expersq | nr", data=wagepan)
mod2.summary()
```

## Different Standard Errors

The point estimates below never change --- only the standard errors do.

### Heteroskedasticity-Robust

```{python}
pf.feols("lwage ~ exper + expersq | nr", data=wagepan, vcov="hetero").summary()
```

### Clustered by Individual

```{python}
pf.feols("lwage ~ exper + expersq | nr", data=wagepan, vcov={"CRV1": "nr"}).summary()
```

### Two-Way Clustered (nr × year)

```{python}
pf.feols("lwage ~ exper + expersq | nr", data=wagepan, vcov={"CRV1": "nr+year"}).summary()
```

## Compare Results

```{python}
mods = {
    "Classical": pf.feols("lwage ~ exper + expersq | nr", data=wagepan, vcov="iid"),
    "Hetero": pf.feols("lwage ~ exper + expersq | nr", data=wagepan, vcov="hetero"),
    "Clustered (id)": pf.feols("lwage ~ exper + expersq | nr", data=wagepan, vcov={"CRV1": "nr"}),
    "Two-way (id+year)": pf.feols("lwage ~ exper + expersq | nr", data=wagepan, vcov={"CRV1": "nr+year"}),
}
pd.DataFrame(
    {name: m.se().round(5) for name, m in mods.items()}
)
```

## Conclusion

- **Clustered SEs** (by individual) are standard in panel wage regressions.
- **Two-way clustering** (id × year) is common when shocks are correlated across both
  dimensions.
